deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated 1847, published posthumously in the Werke, 1876). He studies bilateral series Z(x) = Σ c_α (x−b)^α, where α runs over α0 + Z (all integers added to a fixed, possibly non-integer, exponent). The coefficients are assumed to satisfy the recursion that makes Z proportional to x^μ. The goal is formula (3) (completed on the next page), a generalized Taylor/binomial expansion of x^μ in non-integral powers of (x−b).

(a) End of the footnote begun on p.10. If the integrals are handled before the substitution x = b/y, they become discontinuous at x = 0. Even in that form one sees that the associated constants must be the same for positive and negative x, because the integral varies continuously as x passes from +∞ to −∞ (that is, through infinity).

(b) End of the main sentence from p.10. The integrands (1−y)^{μ−α−1} y^α remain integrable, so the integrals vary continuously, as long as both exponents stay greater than −1. Hence for μ > α > −1:

K = Z(x)·x^{−μ} = p x^{−μ} + p' x^{−μ} = (μ−α) c_α b^{α−μ} ∫_0^1 (1−y)^{μ−α−1} y^α dy = c_α b^{α−μ} Π(α)Π(μ−α)/Π(μ).

Here p, p' are the two half-series (non-negative and negative powers) of Z, each represented by an integral, and Π(s) = Γ(s+1) (Gauss's notation). Implicit step (mine): the integral is the Beta integral B(α+1, μ−α) = Π(α)Π(μ−α−1)/Π(μ), and (μ−α)Π(μ−α−1) = Π(μ−α).

(c) Extension to all α and μ. Define Π of negative arguments by the functional equation Π(n) = Π(n+1)/(n+1). The coefficient recursion is c_{α+1} = (μ−α)c_α/((α+1)b), which follows from x·Z' = μZ (my derivation). It is satisfied by c_α = K Π(μ) b^{μ−α}/(Π(α)Π(μ−α)). So the formula holds for every α in the progression as soon as it holds for one α with −1 < α < μ.

(d) Result for μ > 0:

K x^μ = Σ_{α=−∞}^{∞} K Π(μ) b^{μ−α}(x−b)^α/(Π(α)Π(μ−α)), i.e. x^μ/Π(μ) = Σ_α [b^{μ−α}/Π(μ−α)]·[(x−b)^α/Π(α)].

(e) Next page: n-fold differentiation in x extends this to negative μ, giving formula (3). This is a 'symmetric' generalized Taylor formula: D^{α} x^μ at b, divided appropriately, times (x−b)^α/Π(α).
errors: Convergence: for α→+∞ the term ratio tends to −(x−b)/b, and for α→−∞ it tends to −b/(x−b) in absolute value. So the bilateral series can converge only on the circle |x−b| = |b|, where it converges conditionally given a suitable condition on Re μ. For general x (e.g. real x other than 0 or 2b) formula (3) is not valid as an ordinary sum. Riemann's argument via the integral representations of p and p' and the 'continuity' reasoning does not establish it. He explicitly refuses on p.10 to treat divergence as fatal. This defect was analysed by G. H. Hardy, 'Riemann's form of Taylor's series', J. London Math. Soc. 20 (1945).
Even on |x−b| = |b|, the identity requires a consistent choice of branches for the non-integer powers b^{μ−α}, (x−b)^α and x^μ. This is not discussed.
The identification of K with the integral expressions and the 'singular integrals at y = 0, 1' argument are heuristic. The constancy of K across x = 0 and x = ∞ (footnote) is asserted, not proved.
Minor point: the first expression for K writes p x^{−μ} + p' x^{−μ} where a product with the integral is intended. The equation chain is notationally compressed but the final value is correct.

results.what: Beta-integral evaluation: (μ−α)∫_0^1 (1−y)^{μ−α−1} y^α dy = Π(α)Π(μ−α)/Π(μ) for μ > α > −1
Extension of Π (Gamma) to negative arguments via Π(n) = Π(n+1)/(n+1)
results.modern_name: Analytic continuation of Gamma via the functional equation

results.what: Bilateral expansion x^μ/Π(μ) = Σ_{α∈α0+Z} b^{μ−α}(x−b)^α/(Π(μ−α)Π(α)), extended to all μ (formula (3) of the 'Versuch')
results.modern_name: Riemann's generalized (fractional) Taylor series; related to Dougall's bilateral sum Σ_n 1/(Γ(a+n+1)Γ(b−n+1)) = 2^{a+b}/Γ(a+b+1) and to fractional Taylor series (Hardy 1945; later Osler 1970s)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1847, publ. 1876); corrected and analysed by Hardy (1945)

deep.surprise_reason: This page is part of Riemann's 1847 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation', printed in his Gesammelte Werke (1876). Formula (3), Riemann's form of Taylor's series, is well known as his. Its convergence defect was studied by Hardy (1945). Nothing here goes beyond the published text.

checkable.sympy: simplify((mu-a)*integrate((1-y)**(mu-a-1)*y**a,(y,0,1),conds='none') - gamma(a+1)*gamma(mu-a+1)/gamma(mu+1))  # test numerically with mu=Rational(5,2), a=Rational(1,3)

checkable.asserts: The coefficients satisfy the recursion c_{α+1} = (μ−α)c_α/((α+1)b), which is equivalent to x Z' = μ Z for Z = Σ c_α (x−b)^α
Formula (3) at x = 2b, i.e. (x−b)/b = 1, reduces to Dougall's bilateral sum Σ 1/(Γ(α+1)Γ(μ−α+1)) = 2^μ/Γ(μ+1); here it holds with μ = 3/2
The term ratios tend to |x−b|/|b| and |b|/|x−b|, so the bilateral series can converge only when |x−b| = |b|

transcription_corrections: The integral should read ∫_0^1 (1−y)^{μ−α−1} y^α dy, not ∫_0^b (b−y)^{μ−α−1} ... . This matches p.10 and is needed for the factor b^{α−μ} in the result.

'[-Beide-] Exponenten zu sehr als −1 bleiben' should be read as 'so lange beide Exponenten grösser als −1 bleiben' (continuing the sentence from p.10). 'Beide' is struck and a replacement is written above.
'dass μ > α > −1 und y endlich ist' – the condition is μ > α > −1, i.e. both exponents μ−α−1 and α exceed −1.
The first expression is K = Z·x^{−μ} = p x^{−μ} + p' x^{−μ} = (integral)·(μ−α)c_α b^{α−μ} = c_α b^{α−μ}Π(α)Π(μ−α)/Π(μ). The machine transcription merges the terms incorrectly.
The condition 'einer derselben <μ, >−1' means: some α in the progression satisfies −1 < α < μ.
Margin note: '*) [struck word] (Seite 12)' refers the footnote to p.12.
